description: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts for two categories—“Open” (light blue) and “Cons.” (light pink)—across four essay genres: Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository, with the fourth genre partially cut off but likely corresponding to “Argumentative” or similar based on context from the paper “EssayBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese Essay Writing.” The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to over 120, with major tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis lists the genres. For the “Narrative” genre, the “Open” category has 79 samples and “Cons.” has 122. In “Descriptive,” “Open” has 80 and “Cons.” has 87. For “Expository,” “Open” has 68 and “Cons.” has 100. The final visible genre (partially labeled “Expositor”) shows “Open” at 62 and “Cons.” at 122. The “Cons.” bars consistently exceed the “Open” bars in all visible genres, with the largest difference observed in the first and last categories. The chart uses a grouped bar layout with a legend in the upper right corner identifying the color coding for “Open” and “Cons.” The chart is tilted slightly, giving it a 3D perspective effect, though the data remains clearly readable.
